title: Choose Sentinel’s new visual world
question: Each direction keeps the same product truth, real screenshots, walkthrough, and pilot flow. Choose the world that should make Sentinel unmistakable.

options.label: Release Proof
options.lineage: press-room preflight proofs and registration sheets
options.thesis: The landing page is a release proof waiting for a human sign-off.
options.viewport: One saturated proof sheet fills the first screen; the product run cuts through it as the evidence layer, and the pilot action sits where an approval mark belongs.
options.risk: The production-proof metaphor must stay subordinate to the real product, or it can become graphic-design theatre.

raised.raise: The run trace becomes a real information spine, not a decorative line.
Every claim stays visibly attached to its evidence and human decision point.
The page commits to full-viewport color fields instead of timid accent dots.

options.label: Flight Recorder
options.lineage: aircraft flight strips and incident-recorder traces
options.thesis: One taught journey becomes a trace you can replay, inspect, and trust.
options.viewport: A continuous run trace crosses the first screen, carries the headline inside it, and opens directly into a real evidence view.
options.risk: Flight-recorder language fits the mechanism closely, so it can drift toward the familiar dark observability aesthetic unless kept materially restrained.

options.label: Data-Sublime Field
options.lineage: barcode fields, sine lattices, and high-contrast data art
options.thesis: Sentinel turns each browser journey into an inspectable signal field.
options.viewport: A black-and-white run field fills the screen; the journey trace separates signal from failure while the pilot action remains stark and obvious.
options.case: Strong audience recognition and the most radical departure from the rejected page; slightly weaker at explaining human judgment without supporting copy.
options.risk: The abstraction can overpower the product screenshot and reduce trust if density is not carefully paced.

options.label: Evidence Ribbon
options.thesis: Every test result keeps an unbroken route back to its evidence and owner.
options.viewport: A single evidence ribbon unrolls through the page from taught journey to release decision.
options.case: Product clarity is excellent, but the museum-led language identifies less directly with startup engineering teams.
options.kept: Attach uncertainty and human ownership to every transition.
options.risk: Too much archival language could make Sentinel feel retrospective instead of operational.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished blue SaaS page with a conventional hero, product frame, feature grid, and closing CTA.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and CTA on the left, dashboard screenshot on the right, navigation above.
canonCard.risk: Clear and familiar, but intentionally close to the common website structure you already rejected.
